We propose VideoRouter(VR) that rethinks long-video understanding as coordinating complementary evidence views rather than selecting a single subset of frames. It first organizes each video into a question-agnostic temporal hierarchy, which partition the video into coarse-to-fine temporally coherent segments. In this hierarchy, upper-level nodes capture broad storyline context and event progression, while lower-level nodes preserve fine-grained local details and evidence-bearing moments. This naturally gives rise to two complementary views: a global view for coverage-oriented reasoning and a local view for detail-oriented evidence recovery. We further introduce a verification-guided router to determine which view is better supported by the selected evidence and select the final answer. We validate the effectiveness of the proposed design through extensive experiments, showing that the verification-guided router effectively coordinates global and local reasoning, and that, on VideoMME, our method outperforms state-of-the-art frame selection methods by 2.9 points, respectively, under the LLaVA-Video-7B backbone. We will release the code.

</details>


### [26] [Uncertainty-Aware World Model for Aerial Image-Goal Navigation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05597)
*Deyi Zhu,Haoyu Fan,Yinan Zhu,Weichen Zhang,Shilin Ma,Xinlei Chen,Yansong Tang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Introduces UA-NWM, a latent uncertainty-aware world model for aerial image-goal navigation that scores trajectories via out-of-distribution detection within an uncertainty subspace, enabling robust, sample-efficient planning without multiple future samples, validated in simulators and real UAVs.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current world-model-based trajectory scoring relies on single/multiple point predictions, which fail under large-scale outdoor conditions with significant future-state uncertainty.

Method: Define UA-NWM: a latent world model that represents plausible futures with an uncertainty subspace, decomposes the prediction–goal discrepancy into uncertainty-explainable and unexplainable components, and uses only the unexplainable residual for scoring to achieve robust trajectory selection without sampling multiple futures.

Result: Outperforms existing navigation world models in both simulations and real UAV experiments while maintaining low inference latency.

Conclusion: Uncertainty-aware latent modeling improves robustness and efficiency for aerial image-goal navigation, with demonstrated practicality in real-world deployments.

Abstract: Aerial image-goal navigation requires an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to reach a target location specified by a goal image. Existing world-model-based methods rank candidate trajectories using predicted futures, but typically rely on only one or a few point predictions, which is inadequate for large-scale outdoor environments with substantial future-state uncertainty. To address this limitation, we propose the Uncertainty-Aware Navigation World Model (UA-NWM), an efficient latent world model for aerial image-goal navigation, which formulates trajectory scoring as conditional out-of-distribution detection. UA-NWM represents plausible futures with an uncertainty subspace and decomposes the prediction--goal discrepancy into uncertainty-explainable and unexplainable components. Only the unexplainable residual is used for scoring, enabling robust selection without multiple future samples. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UA-NWM consistently outperforms existing navigation world models while maintaining low inference latency. Real-world UAV experiments further validate its practical applicability. Project page: https://duryi.github.io/UA-NWM-Project-Page

</details>


### [27] [ALTER: Modeling Longitudinal Changes via Regional Differencing for 3D CT Report Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05615)
*Dongchen Li,Jitao Liang,Wei Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ALTER: a CT report generation framework leveraging global priors and region-specific longitudinal evidence to capture interval changes across regions, achieving state-of-the-art results on chest CT datasets.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Clinical CT reporting requires capturing patient-specific longitudinal changes across anatomical regions, not just per-exam detail; existing methods miss cross-region interval changes and context from prior exams.

Method: Global Prior Integration (GPI) to incorporate prior CT and report; Regional Proxy Differencing (RPD) to obtain per-region historical proxies from a shared prior encoding; Interval Change Fusion (ICF) to fuse current abnormalities with regional differences into change-aware soft prompts guiding report generation.

Result: State-of-the-art on RadGenome-ChestCT validation and CTRG-Chest-548K test; code and preprocessing details available at GitHub.

Conclusion: ALTER effectively models longitudinal, regional interval changes and improves radiology report generation; potential for broader clinical uptake with open resources.

Abstract: Computed tomography (CT) is widely used for clinical diagnosis and longitudinal follow-up, yet automatically generating accurate and complete radiology reports from three-dimensional (3D) CT remains challenging. Existing methods improve fine-grained correspondence between images and text by modeling anatomical regions, but remain centered on the current examination. Consequently, patient-specific longitudinal changes within individual regions remain insufficiently modeled. Meanwhile, interval changes are often distributed across multiple anatomical regions, complicating a coherent assessment of the overall longitudinal state. We propose Anatomically Localized Temporal Evidence Representation (ALTER) to address these limitations. Global Prior Integration (GPI) incorporates the prior CT and report to establish historical context for the current examination. Regional Proxy Differencing (RPD) enables each current anatomical region to retrieve a historical proxy from a single shared encoding of the prior volume and to derive localized interval evidence. Interval Change Fusion (ICF) further combines current abnormality states with region-distributed differences, converting their joint representation into change-aware soft prompts that guide report generation. ALTER achieves state-of-the-art results on most evaluation metrics across the RadGenome-ChestCT validation and CTRG-Chest-548K test sets. Code and data preprocessing details are available at https://github.com/peytonkarlie/ALTER/tree/main.

</details>


### [28] [TruthLens: Object Hallucination Detection via Self-Evaluating Truthfulness Scores in LVLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05616)
*Yanqi Wu,Runhe Lai,Xinhua Lu,Qichao Chen,Zhiping Zhou,Jia-Xin Zhuang,Weijiang Yu,Ruixuan Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: TruthLens is a self-evaluation framework that uses a rare reference token to extract a truthfulness signal from the LM head, fine-tuning with an MSE objective to separate real vs hallucinated objects, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy with negligible inference cost and good generalization.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Object hallucination in LVLMs; separability of real vs hallucinated tokens in hidden representations is lost at the LM head; need a low-cost, self-contained method to reveal truthfulness without extra models.

Method: Repurpose a rarely-used special token as a reference token. For each object-token position, take the LM head's log-probability of the reference token; define truthfulness as the deviation from a constant; fine-tune the LM head with an MSE objective to drive scores toward 1 for real objects and 0 for hallucinations, with a divergence constraint to preserve generation capability. Trained on a limited set of object categories; generalizes to larger label spaces.

Result: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple LVLMs; e.g., on Qwen2.5-VL-7B, AUROC on MS-COCO improves by >17 percentage points over prior best. Demonstrates strong generalization to larger label spaces. Code released.

Conclusion: TruthLens provides a lightweight, self-contained mechanism to expose object truthfulness signals at the LM head, enabling reliable detection of hallucinations without additional models or inference cost, with good generalization.

Abstract: Despite the remarkable progress of large vision language models (LVLMs), object hallucination remains a fundamental challenge that hinders their trustworthy deployment. A key finding motivates our work: real and hallucinated object tokens are clearly separable in hidden representations, yet this separability is largely lost at the language-modeling (LM) head. We propose TruthLens, a self-evaluation framework that teaches the LM head to expose a per-object truthfulness signal without any auxiliary model or additional inference cost. Concretely, a rarely-used special token is repurposed as a reference token. For each object-token position, we extract the log-probability assigned to this special token by the LM head, and define its difference from a predefined constant as the truthfulness score. The model is then fine-tuned with an MSE objective that drives scores toward 1 for real objects and 0 for hallucinated ones, while a divergence constraint preserves the original generation capability. Despite being trained on only a limited set of object categories, TruthLens generalizes effectively to benchmarks with substantially larger label spaces. Extensive experiments across multiple LVLMs demonstrate state-of-the-art performance; notably, on Qwen2.5-VL-7B, TruthLens outperforms the previous best method on MS-COCO by over 17\% in AUROC. Our code is available at https://github.com/wyqstan/TruthLens.

</details>


### [29] [Dual-Output Multi-Exposure HDR Reconstruction via SDR Fusion and Gain Map Inverse Tone Mapping](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05626)
*Jinho Kim,Jinwoo Kim,Seon Joo Kim*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: DOME-HDR jointly reconstructs an SDR and a consistent HDR from three bracketed LDR images using a LoRA-adapted latent diffusion base for SDR and a dual cross-attention fusion to integrate under-/over-exposed cues anchored to mid exposure, followed by an HDR Prior-guided Gain Map network to generate a spatially varying gain map for HDR expansion, achieving state-of-the-art results on standard datasets with ablations validating key components.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: HDR reconstruction from bracketed LDR inputs often faces trade-offs between preserving structural detail and color fidelity while expanding dynamic range. Existing methods may struggle to produce both perceptually balanced SDRs and consistent HDRs. The work aims to jointly optimize SDR synthesis and HDR gain-map estimation to improve both perceptual quality and dynamic-range expansion.

Method: 1) Synthesize a base SDR from three LDR inputs using a LoRA-adapted latent diffusion model. 2) Use a dual cross-attention fusion module to fuse structural and color cues from under- and over-exposed images, anchored by the mid exposure for stability. 3) Use the synthesized SDR to guide HPGM (HDR Prior-guided Gain Map network) to predict a spatially varying gain map for reliable dynamic-range expansion and HDR reconstruction via gain-map inversion.

Result: Evaluations on Kalantari, Tel, and Challenge123 using full-reference and no-reference metrics show state-of-the-art HDR reconstruction quality. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of the dual cross-attention fusion and SDR-guided gain map estimation.

Conclusion: DOME-HDR effectively and jointly optimizes SDR synthesis and HDR expansion from bracketed LDR inputs, with dual cross-attention fusion and SDR guidance contributing to state-of-the-art performance and robustness across datasets.

Abstract: We propose DOME-HDR, a dual-output multi-exposure HDR reconstruction framework that jointly produces a perceptually balanced SDR image and a consistent HDR image via gain map inverse tone mapping. Given three bracketed LDR inputs, DOME-HDR first synthesizes a base SDR using a LoRA-adapted latent diffusion model. A dual cross-attention fusion module injects complementary structural and color cues from the under- and over-exposed images while anchoring on the mid exposure for stability. The synthesized SDR then guides HPGM, our HDR Prior-guided Gain Map network, to predict a spatially varying gain map for reliable dynamic-range expansion. We evaluate on Kalantari, Tel, and Challenge123 using both full-reference and no-reference metrics, where DOME-HDR achieves state-of-the-art HDR reconstruction quality; ablations further confirm the effectiveness of dual cross-attention and SDR-guided gain map estimation.

</details>


### [30] [SCI-CLIP: Segment-Centric Inference with Reference Memory for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05627)
*Mohamad Zamini,Diksha Shukla*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A training-free, region-centric framework (SCI-CLIP) converts frozen CLIP features into dense, spatially coherent open-vocabulary predictions by building a region interaction graph, graph-based feature reconstruction, cross-window support, and an offline exemplar memory, yielding improved dense segmentation across eight benchmarks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address the lack of a unified inference abstraction in training-free open-vocabulary segmentation. Patch-level frozen features cannot directly support dense prediction; a single region-based abstraction is needed to govern feature interaction, spatial support, contextual recovery, and retrieval-based corrections.

Method: Construct a region-consistent interaction graph over frozen visual tokens, propagate values on this graph to reconstruct dense features, and augment with selective cross-window support where local evidence is insufficient. Use the same region abstraction to build and query an offline reference memory for exemplar retrieval aligned with the prediction units. All steps run without training.

Result: SCI-CLIP improves the structural quality of dense predictions, strengthens contextual reasoning, and improves alignment of exemplar-based corrections, achieving stronger open-vocabulary segmentation across eight benchmarks. Code is available at the provided GitHub link.

Conclusion: SCI-CLIP shows that frozen CLIP features can be transformed into spatially coherent, context-aware, and retrieval-compatible dense predictions without training, enabling robust open-vocabulary segmentation.

Abstract: Training-free open-vocabulary segmentation remains limited by a missing inference abstraction. Frozen vision-language features are produced at patch level, yet dense prediction requires a unit that simultaneously governs feature interaction, spatial support, contextual recovery, and retrieval-based correction. We present SCI-CLIP, a segment-centric inference framework built around the principle that the same region abstraction should organize all stages of dense open-vocabulary prediction. SCI-CLIP first induces a region-consistent interaction graph over frozen visual tokens, then reconstructs dense features by propagating values over this graph, augmenting them with selective cross-window support only where local evidence is insufficient. The same segment abstraction is subsequently used to construct and query an offline reference memory, aligning exemplar retrieval with the units on which prediction is made. SCI-CLIP turns frozen CLIP-style features into spatially coherent, context-aware, and retrieval-compatible dense predictions without any training. SCI-CLIP consistently improves the structural quality of dense predictions, the robustness of contextual reasoning, and the alignment of exemplar-based correction, yielding stronger open-vocabulary segmentation across eight benchmarks. Project code is available at: https://github.com/mzamini92/SCICLIP.

</details>


### [31] [ChronoVision: Temporal Reasoning via Latent State Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05631)
*Yifan Shen,Jian Xu,Boyi Li,Yuner Zhang,Tianjiao Yu,Bingxuan Li,Houze Yang,Rushi Wang,Xu Cao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ChronoVision aligns visual logic with latent imagery to enhance temporal visual reasoning in multimodal LLMs.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To overcome the degradation in temporal reasoning caused by the ambiguity of language-based reasoning when describing continuous visual transformations.

Method: Supervised fine-tuning with a Reconstructive Visual Head predicting the latent final state and an ROI Attention Locating module using semantic span queries; post-training reinforcement learning with an implicit process grounding mechanism and a composite reward for outcome correctness, latent process alignment, and unsupervised focus.

Result: Achieves state-of-the-art on Vbvr-VQA (74.8% in-domain, 71.6% out-of-domain) and strong 55.0% accuracy on IntPhys2.

Conclusion: ChronoVision effectively improves temporal visual reasoning by aligning latent imagery with visual logic and focusing evidence; the Vbvr-VQA dataset provides a stringent benchmark for temporal reasoning tasks.

Abstract: Multimodal large language models excel at passive perception but struggle with complex visual cognitive tasks requiring multi-step temporal reasoning. This degradation largely stems from the inherent ambiguity of language-based reasoning, which often fails to accurately articulate continuous visual transformations. To address this, we propose ChronoVision, a multimodal framework designed to align visual logic with latent imagery. During supervised fine-tuning, a Reconstructive Visual Head predicts the latent representation of the final transformed state, while an ROI Attention Locating module focuses the model on key visual evidence via semantic span queries. In post-training, we apply reinforcement learning with an implicit process grounding mechanism, guided by a composite reward function that evaluates outcome correctness, latent process alignment, and unsupervised visual focus. Furthermore, we introduce Vbvr-VQA, a novel dataset that evaluates temporal tracking by reformulating video reasoning into a strict image-ordering task. Experiments demonstrate that ChronoVision achieves state-of-the-art performance on Vbvr-VQA with 74.8% in-domain and 71.6% out-of-domain accuracy, alongside a strong 55.0% accuracy on IntPhys2, a highly challenging cross-domain benchmark.

</details>


### [32] [Vorch-IR: Long-Form Unified Multimodal Identity Replacement Video Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05648)
*Yaole Wang,Xiaoyu Chen,Xin Ma,Yang Ding,Gang Yue,Jingjing Chen,Lin Ma,Yaohui Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Vorch-IR is a unified framework for single- and dual-person video identity replacement (with optional background replacement) that conditions on a driving video, index references, and a text instruction; it uses self-attention for visual fusion and cross-attention for language grounding, includes automatic data synthesis for paired supervision, and introduces temporal overlapping inference to enable minute-scale generation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Prior work is largely single-person, relies on task-specific controls (e.g., masks, pose representations), and suffers from scarce paired data for multi-person editing, limiting flexible, multimodal video editing and generalization.

Method: Vorch-IR is built on LTX2 and takes as input a driving video, indexed reference images, and a textual editing instruction. The instruction designates the roles of references (subject vs. background). Visual fusion uses dense self-attention; semantic alignment uses cross-attention with the text. An automatic data construction pipeline synthesizes paired supervision for four editing settings (single/dual identities, with/without background). Temporal overlapping inference extends short clips to minute-scale generation without autoregressive continuation.

Result: Experiments with automatic metrics and human pairwise evaluation show strong identity preservation, motion fidelity, and temporal coherence across diverse scenarios.

Conclusion: The work delivers a unified, flexible approach for single- and dual-person identity replacement with optional background editing in a single model; it supports mismatched reference poses/layouts via instruction-guided role assignment, provides a data-synthesis pipeline to reduce supervision requirements, and enables long-horizon generation through temporal overlapping inference.

Abstract: Video identity replacement seeks to transfer the identities of one or more subjects while preserving the motion, expressions, and temporal structure of a driving video. Existing methods largely target single-person settings and often require task-specific structural controls, such as masks or pose representations, limiting their flexibility in general multimodal editing systems. Progress on multi-person replacement is further constrained by the scarcity of paired training data. We present Vorch-IR, a unified framework that supports single- and dual-person identity replacement, with optional background replacement, in a single model. Built on LTX2, Vorch-IR jointly conditions on a driving video, indexed reference images, and a textual editing instruction. The reference images need not match the pose, layout, or spatial configuration of the driving video: their roles as subject or background references are specified through the instruction. Dense visual conditions are fused through self-attention, while a vision-language context establishes semantic correspondence through cross-attention. We further develop an automatic data construction pipeline that synthesizes paired supervision for all four editing settings. Experiments using automatic metrics and pairwise human evaluation demonstrate strong identity preservation, motion fidelity, and temporal coherence across diverse scenarios. A temporal overlapping inference strategy additionally extends the short-clip model to minute-long generation without autoregressive continuation.

</details>


### [33] [Vorch-Streamer: Extending Human Audio-Visual Generation to Real-Time Long-Form Streaming](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05663)
*Menglin Han,Yang Ding,Yulei Lu,Haoran Yu,Xin Ma,Junyi Chen,Zhangkai Ni,Lin Ma,Yaohui Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Vorch-Streamer enables real-time long-form T2AV streaming by combining causal generation with diffusion-based synthesis, long-horizon self-forcing (DMD distillation), and an external 25 Hz speech-planning model to align content with speech, achieving 27.12 FPS while preserving lip-sync and identity.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Real-time avatar generation requires causal, continuous audio-video synthesis with tight audiovisual synchronization. Adapting pretrained bidirectional models risks exposure bias and ambiguous speech progression under limited context.

Method: Create a synthetic 80k-clip corpus (12–21s). Train a causal generator with mixed Teacher Forcing and Diffusion Forcing. Apply long-horizon Self Forcing with DMD distillation. Use an external language model to predict discrete 25 Hz speech-planning tokens; condition the audio diffusion branch on these tokens. Employ bounded causal context with four-step denoising for joint audio-video generation.

Result: Real-time generation at 27.12 FPS (surpassing 24 FPS playback), with competitive audio–lip synchronization and strong identity preservation across long-form content.

Conclusion: Vorch-Streamer offers a practical post-training solution to realize real-time long-form T2AV streaming, mitigating exposure bias and aligning speech progression with content while maintaining audiovisual fidelity.

Abstract: Real-time long-form avatar audio--video generation requires causal, continuous synthesis while maintaining audiovisual synchronization and visual consistency. Adapting a pretrained bidirectional model to this setting presents two key dilemmas. First, autoregressively reusing generated blocks as context creates exposure bias, causing errors and visual drift to accumulate over long rollouts. Second, a global speech utterance does not indicates a causal generator which portion should be spoken next when only limited local audio--video context is available. We present \textbf{Vorch-Streamer}, a post-training framework that addresses these challenges and enables real-time long-form Text-to-Audio-Video (T2AV) streaming. We construct a synthetic corpus of 80K avatar clips spanning 12--21 seconds and first train a causal generator with mixed Teacher Forcing and Diffusion Forcing. We then apply long-horizon Self Forcing with DMD distillation, exposing the model to its own rollout distribution while preserving the quality of the pretrained bidirectional teacher. To explicitly control speech progression, an external language model predicts discrete 25-Hz speech-planning tokens, whose continuous features condition the audio diffusion branch and align each causal block with the content it should speak. With bounded causal context and four-step denoising, Vorch-Streamer jointly generates audio and video from text at 27.12 FPS, exceeding the 24-FPS real-time playback rate while maintaining competitive audio--lip synchronization and strong identity preservation over long-form generation.

</details>


### [34] [Dual-Attention and Adversarial Transfer Networks for Sim-to-Real Cross-Orientation Wireless Sensing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05664)
*Linfeng Du,Kehan Wu,Tong Zhang,Rui Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Physics-guided S2M-Sense simulator synthesizes orientation-diverse mmWave data from single-orientation motion; a dual-attention network extracts orientation-robust features from dual-link Doppler spectrograms; unsupervised adversarial transfer learning aligns simulated and real features with few unlabeled samples, achieving high accuracy and outperforming cross-domain methods.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Performance degradation in mmWave HAR due to user orientation; collecting labeled multi-orientation data is costly; need simulation-to-reality bridging.

Method: Physics-guided simulator producing orientation-diverse training data from single orientation; dual-attention network for activity-discriminative and orientation-robust representations from dual-link Doppler spectrograms; adversarial unsupervised transfer learning to align feature distributions using minimal unlabeled target samples.

Result: SSIM 0.84 between simulated and measured Doppler spectrograms across 4 activities and 4 orientations; 88.33% recognition accuracy with simulated data; 95% after transfer learning with 16 unlabeled samples; outperforming state-of-the-art cross-domain methods.

Conclusion: Integrating physics-guided synthesis, dual-attention features, and unsupervised transfer learning effectively mitigates orientation-induced variations in mmWave HAR and enhances cross-domain performance.

Abstract: Millimeter-wave human activity recognition suffers significant performance degradation when the user's orientation changes relative to the sensing system, yet collecting labeled multi-orientation data is labor-intensive and costly. To eliminate the need for exhaustive multi-orientation measured data, we develop a physics-guided simulator that synthesizes orientation-diverse wireless training data from single-orientation motion. Specifically, to suppress orientation-induced feature variations, we propose a dual-attention network that extracts activity-discriminative and orientation-robust representations from dual-link Doppler spectrograms. To bridge the simulation-to-reality gap, we introduce an adversarial unsupervised transfer learning mechanism that aligns feature distributions using only a small number of unlabeled target-domain samples. The S2M-Sense platform shows high fidelity in reproducing real-world signatures, validated against 60.48 GHz mmWave measured data with an average structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of 0.84 between simulated and measured Doppler spectrograms across all 4 activities and 4 orientations. Experimental results show that S2M-Sense achieves 88.33% recognition accuracy using only the dual-link multi-orientation simulated dataset, which improves to 95% after simulation-to-reality transfer learning with as few as 16 unlabeled measured samples. Both cases with and without transfer learning outperform state-of-the-art cross-domain sensing methods.

</details>


### [35] [URNet: A Unified Reparameterized Network for Efficient RGB-D Semantic Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05671)
*Guoan Xu,Zhengxue Wang,Yang Xiao,Ligeng Chen,Guangwei Gao,Dongchen Zhu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: URNet is a unified RGB-D network that performs joint feature extraction and fusion in a single reparameterized encoder, with a Linear Gated Attention module in RepBlocks and a Pyramid Merging Decoder, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy with high efficiency.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Dual-branch RGB-D designs with separate encoders often fail to capture depth representations and cross-modal interactions effectively, while adding an extra encoder increases computation, hindering lightweight deployment.

Method: A single-encoder URNet with Reparameterized Blocks (RepBlocks) incorporating Linear Gated Attention (LGA) to fuse RGB-depth cues across scales, plus a lightweight Pyramid Merging Decoder (PMD) for multi-scale decoding and fusion.

Result: Extensive experiments on multiple RGB-D segmentation benchmarks show state-of-the-art performance with high efficiency; code will be released.

Conclusion: URNet demonstrates effective unified multi-modal processing; the LGA within RepBlocks and the PMD decoder contribute to accurate, efficient RGB-D segmentation and suggest a path toward streamlined cross-modal architectures.

Abstract: Previous RGB-D semantic segmentation methods commonly employ dual encoders to separately process RGB and depth inputs, followed by dedicated modules for cross-modal feature fusion. However, such designs often inadequately capture depth representations and consequently limit effective cross-modal interaction, while the additional encoder branch introduces redundant computation that hinders lightweight execution. To tackle these challenges, we propose URNet, a Unified Reparameterized RGB-D Network that performs simultaneous multi-modal feature extraction and cross-modal fusion within a single encoder. Specifically, we adopt a reparameterization strategy to compact the network architecture and facilitate fast inference. Within each Reparameterized Block (RepBlock), a Linear Gated Attention (LGA) module is introduced to fully exploit complementary RGB and depth cues across different feature scales. Furthermore, considering that decoder design has been relatively underexplored in existing RGB-D segmentation models, we develop a concise yet effective universal decoder, termed the Pyramid Merging Decoder (PMD). Extensive experiments on multiple RGB-D segmentation benchmarks demonstrate that URNet achieves state-of-the-art performance while maintaining high efficiency. Code will be available at https://github.com/Wild-Stephen/URNet.

</details>


### [36] [DistMedVL: Distributional Vision-Language Alignment for Uncertainty-Aware Medical Image Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05683)
*Jiaxuan Li,Qing Xu,Xiangjian He,Yue Li,Daokun Zhang,Fiseha B. Tesema,Rong Qu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A lightweight probabilistic cross-modal alignment framework for medical image segmentation that models uncertainty via a probabilistic adapter (PCM-Adapter) with Mahalanobis-based alignment and a distribution flow module, improving robustness and data efficiency.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Cross-modal misalignment and uncertainty (aleatoric and epistemic) hinder vision-language medical segmentation, especially under domain shift; prior methods use deterministic matching.

Method: Freeze encoders; insert PCM-Adapter with two modules: MAM models textual tokens as Gaussian distributions and uses Mahalanobis distance for patch-text compatibility with variance-aware weighting; DFM estimates modality-wise confidences and refines textual distributions guided by visual modality; end-to-end training involves probabilistic representations with limited parameters (6.3M).

Result: On eight medical segmentation benchmarks, DistMedVL achieves state-of-the-art performance with only 6.3M trainable parameters, showing enhanced data efficiency, robustness to perturbations, and cross-dataset generalization.

Conclusion: Probabilistic cross-modal alignment improves reliability of vision-language segmentation in medical imaging; the approach offers a lightweight, robust alternative to deterministic methods, effectively handling boundary ambiguity and domain shifts.

Abstract: Cross-modal alignment of visual and textual representations is fundamental to multimodal medical image understanding, yet remains hindered by uncertainty in both modalities under real-world clinical conditions. Existing vision-language segmentation methods rely on deterministic cross-modal matching, which overlooks aleatoric uncertainty from ambiguous boundaries and epistemic uncertainty from limited training data, leading to fragile performance under domain shift. To address this issue, we propose DistMedVL, a probabilistic vision-language framework that introduces a lightweight Probabilistic Cross-Modal Adapter (PCM-Adapter) upon frozen encoders to explicitly model representational uncertainty. Specifically, the PCM-Adapter comprises two sequential modules for progressive probabilistic alignment. We first devise a Mahalanobis Alignment Module (MAM) that models textual tokens as Gaussian distributions and computes patch-text compatibility via Mahalanobis distance, yielding variance-conditioned matching that downweights unreliable feature dimensions. Moreover, we devise a Distribution Flow Module (DFM) that estimates modality-wise confidence parameters and performs vision-guided refinement of textual distributions, accommodating distributional variation across imaging modalities. Extensive experiments across eight medical segmentation benchmarks demonstrate that DistMedVL outperforms state-of-the-art methods with only 6.3M trainable parameters, exhibiting superior data efficiency, perturbation robustness and cross-dataset generalization.

</details>


### [37] [Shape-Aware Oriented Bounding Box (OBB) to Horizontal Bounding Box (HBB) Conversion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05858)
*Badha Rathna Sabhapathy,Gotam Dahiya,Vishesh Vatsal*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Shape-aware OBB-to-HBB conversion improves tightness of axis-aligned boxes for ship detection in remote sensing by using hull geometry and orientation; benchmarked against three baseline conversions.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: OBB offer tighter fits than HBB; conventional OBB-to-HBB conversions can introduce background or data loss; a geometry-informed conversion is needed to preserve detection quality in aerial imagery.

Method: Introduce a shape-aware OBB-to-HBB conversion that leverages hull shape, hull fullness, and the bounding box orientation to produce a tighter axis-aligned HBB. Compare against three baselines: Outer HBB (min/max), Area Equivalent HBB, and GBB Marginalized HBB.

Result: The method is benchmarked against three baseline OBB-to-HBB conversions; the abstract does not provide quantitative results.

Conclusion: A shape-aware OBB-to-HBB conversion can yield tighter axis-aligned HBBs for ships in remote sensing imagery, potentially improving post-processing and detection quality; validated by benchmarking against three baselines.

Abstract: Accurate object detection in aerial and satellite imagery is dependent upon the bounding box representation. This is especially true for spatially oriented objects such as ships or aircrafts. Oriented Bounding Boxes (OBB) have a tighter fit and more robust non-max suppression compared to Horizontal Bounding Boxes (HBB), any current post-processing conversion from OBB to HBB either introduces excess empty and background space or removes data from the detection. This paper introduces a novel approach for a shape-aware OBB-to-HBB conversion for ship detection in remote sensing imagery. It leverages hull shape, hull fullness, and the bounding box orientation to produce a tighter axis-aligned HBB representation. The proposed method is benchmarked against three baselines methods for OBBto-HBB conversion, Outer HBB which uses minimum and maximum, Area Equivalent HBB and GBB Marginalized HBB.

</details>


### [38] [SciQNet: Two-Stage Multimodal Adaptation for Scientific Image Quality Assessment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05691)
*Yin-Loon Khor,Yi-Jie Wong,Jing Jie Tan,Ming Jie Lee*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: SciQNet: a two-stage domain-adaptive multimodal framework for scientific image quality assessment that achieves top performance and 2nd place in ICME 2026.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Addresses the challenge of evaluating scientific image quality by exploiting domain-adaptive pretraining on scientific documents and task-specific joint supervision.

Method: Stage 1 domain-adaptive pretraining on scientific document images; Stage 2 fine-tuning with joint scoring and understanding supervision: scoring via instruction tuning + Huber loss from rating-word logits; understanding via multiple-choice VQA.

Result: Final model achieves SIQA-S 92.21, SIQA-U 47.38, combined 69.80; ranked 2nd in ICME 2026 Scientific Image Quality Assessment Challenge scoring track.

Conclusion: Domain-adaptive pretraining data relevance significantly impacts performance; the two-stage setup effectively combines scoring and understanding to boost quality assessment of scientific images.

Abstract: Scientific images are essential for communicating experimental observations, quantitative evidence and conceptual knowledge. Unlike natural images, their quality depends on both visual clarity and scientific informativeness, making assessment challenging. In this work, we present SciQNet, a two-stage multimodal adaptation framework for scientific image quality assessment. The first stage performs domain-adaptive pretraining on scientific document images and the second stage conducts task-specific fine-tuning with joint scoring and understanding supervision. For scoring-oriented supervision, we combine instruction tuning with a Huber loss derived from rating-word logits, while understanding-oriented supervision is formulated as multiple-choice visual question answering. Experiments show that using a 40% stratified subset of the domain-adaptive data gives the best performance among the evaluated pretraining fractions, suggesting that pretraining-data relevance may be as important as pretraining-data scale. The final model achieves an SIQA-S score of 92.21, an SIQA-U score of 47.38 and a combined score of 69.80. This work presents our solution to the ICME 2026 Scientific Image Quality Assessment Challenge, which ranked 2nd in the scoring track.

</details>


### [39] [Robust-WAM: Bridging Generative Pretraining and Semantic Foresight in World-Action Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05903)
*Haodong Yan,Junfeng Li,Junjie He,Zhide Zhong,MingMing Yu,Wenxuan Song,Jiaguan Zhu,Yangyang Zheng,Yuqiao Du,Jiadi You,Yingjie Cai,Xu Yan,Guanyi Zhao,Bingbing Liu,Haoang Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Introduces Robust-WAM, a post-training method that preserves VAE-based video generation paths while adding semantic foresight alignment to improve out-of-distribution generalization in video-generation-based world-action models (WAMs).


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: VAE latent space prioritizes pixel reconstruction, which can degrade action prediction under appearance shifts; semantic latent space is more robust to visual changes but lacks large-scale VGM pretraining available in VAE space. Need to combine the strengths of both.

Method: Maintain the VAE-based generative path and add a lightweight semantic foresight alignment on the action stream using learnable query tokens that extract future-scene semantics. Each query is temporally aligned with its corresponding future action via the positional encoding of the matching action token, linking predicted actions to future frames.

Result: Robust-WAM yields consistent improvements in success rates for multiple WAM baselines on out-of-distribution benchmarks and a real-robot setup, without sacrificing in-distribution performance.

Conclusion: The approach grounds actions in appearance-invariant dynamics while preserving large-scale VGM pretraining, enhancing robustness to illumination shifts and visual OOD conditions.

Abstract: Mainstream World-Action Models (WAMs) adapt pretrained video generation models (VGMs) for robot control, transferring their learned dynamics prior for action prediction. These VGMs are typically trained in a variational autoencoder (VAE) latent space. However, the VAE latent space is optimized for pixel reconstruction, which rewards fine appearance detail and leaves the action prediction fragile under visual shifts. Recent works build WAMs in semantic latent space, which are more robust to appearance shifts. However, these models cannot leverage the large-scale VGM pretraining that exists only in VAE space. To overcome this dilemma, we propose Robust-WAM, a general post-training method for video-generation-based WAMs that preserves the VAE-based generative path and adds a lightweight semantic foresight alignment objective on the action stream. This retains the large-scale VGM pretraining while grounding actions in appearance-invariant dynamics that stay reliable under illumination shifts and other visual out-of-distribution conditions. Specifically, we employ learnable query tokens to bring future-scene semantics into the action stream by aligning their output hidden states with the semantic foresight of future ground-truth frames. To establish the temporal correspondence between each query and the future step it describes, we give it the positional encoding of the matching action tokens. Experiments on out-of-distribution generalization simulation benchmarks and a real-robot setup show that our Robust-WAM consistently improves the success rates of multiple WAM baselines without sacrificing in-distribution performance.

</details>


### [40] [TAU-Bench: From Anomaly Instance Tracking to Fine-Grained Video Anomaly Understanding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05699)
*Kepeng Yang,Dongxuan Liu,Rongxin Gao,Zixin Su,Rui Wu,Shuzhao Xie,Chenxin Li,Panwang Pan,Yuzhi Huang,Yue Huang,Jingyan Jiang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: TAU-Bench is a track-centric benchmark for joint anomaly instance tracking and fine-grained anomaly understanding in videos, highlighting gaps between semantic reasoning and visual grounding in current VLMs.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current video anomaly understanding benchmarks evaluate tracking and semantic understanding separately, failing to measure instance-level grounding and coherent temporal narratives; a joint evaluation is needed to assess reliability and grounding.

Method: An automated data engine constructs TAU-Bench by anomaly suitability filtering, anomaly instance track construction, hierarchical caption annotation, and human quality control. TAU-Bench includes 1,118 videos, 1,454 tracks, and 202,438 pixel-level masks across 49 event and 45 scene categories, with track-centric annotations linking instance identification, event understanding, and scene reasoning; evaluations span representative vision-language model families.

Result: Findings show that models can generate plausible anomaly descriptions yet fail to localize and consistently track the correct instance, revealing a persistent gap between semantic reasoning and visual grounding; highlights the need for instance-grounded evaluation.

Conclusion: TAU-Bench advances VAU by enabling joint tracking and fine-grained understanding, promoting faithful and reliable anomaly understanding systems through instance-grounded evaluation and scalable data construction.

Abstract: Humans understand anomalous events through a coherent perceptual process in which they identify the focal instance, follow its behavior as the event unfolds, and interpret why it violates the expectations of the surrounding scene. Video anomaly understanding (VAU) seeks to endow models with a similar capability, moving beyond deciding whether a video is anomalous toward explaining how the event develops and why it matters. Although recent vision--language models (VLMs) can generate detailed and plausible anomaly descriptions, their semantic fluency does not ensure that these interpretations remain grounded in the correct anomaly instance over time. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate tracking and semantic understanding through separate protocols, leaving such instance--semantic inconsistency largely unmeasured. We therefore introduce TAU-Bench, a track-centric benchmark for jointly evaluating anomaly instance tracking and fine-grained anomaly understanding. TAU-Bench contains 1,118 videos, 1,454 tracks, and 202,438 pixel-level masks spanning 49 event and 45 scene categories, together with track-centric annotations that connect instance-level identification, event-level understanding, and scene-level reasoning. To build TAU-Bench at scale, we developed an automated data engine integrating anomaly suitability filtering, anomaly instance track construction, hierarchical caption annotation, and human quality control. Evaluations across representative VLM families show that models producing plausible anomaly interpretations may still fail to localize and track the correct instance reliably, revealing a persistent gap between semantic reasoning and visual grounding. These findings therefore highlight instance-grounded evaluation as an important step toward more faithful and reliable VAU systems.

</details>


### [41] [StreamArena: Toward Continuous, Interactive, and Long-Horizon Agentic Streaming Video Understanding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05703)
*Xichen Zhang,Guankai Li,Yinghao Zhu,Shijian Wang,Sitong Wu,Shaozuo Yu,Meng Chu,Yuan Lu,Jiaya Jia*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: StreamArena provides an hour-scale streaming video benchmark and StreamMind a two-tier system that balances real-time interaction with persistent multimodal memory to improve long-horizon understanding.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current evaluations rely on short clips and fail to evaluate long-horizon, continuous streaming perception and proactive tool use; need benchmarks and architectures that support unbounded audio-visual streams with hour-scale memory.

Method: Introduce StreamArena with 243 full-length videos (~88.8 min) and 3,646 open-ended QA pairs; propose StreamMind with frontend latency-focused workers and backend memory-building workers; enable persistent memory, recall, and external search.

Result: StreamMind outperforms existing streaming baselines across the four capabilities; reduces query-to-answer latency by reusing persistent state; exposes tension between continuous interaction and long-horizon comprehension.

Conclusion: Two-tier architecture that separates latency-sensitive interaction from memory-building components enables effective hour-scale streaming video understanding and demonstrates the value of persistent multimodal memory for long-horizon tasks.

Abstract: Deploying autonomous multimodal agents in continuous, real-world environments requires them to ingest unbounded audio-visual streams and maintain hour-scale memory. However, current evaluations predominantly rely on brief clips and multiple-choice formats. This design allows minimal baselines that process only the last four frames to match or surpass complex streaming models, while answer options also expose language shortcuts. We introduce StreamArena, a benchmark for hour-scale, interactive streaming video understanding. StreamArena contains 243 full-length videos averaging 88.8 minutes and 3,646 rigorously annotated, open-ended question-answer pairs that evaluate real-time perception, historical retrospection, proactive interaction, and multimodal tool utilization. Evaluation across diverse systems exposes a tension between continuous interaction and long-horizon multimodal comprehension. Methods that retain only recent frames cannot recover distant events, methods that convert past observations into text lose visual evidence, and methods that repeatedly compress visual memory struggle to preserve fine-grained details over time. We address this tension with StreamMind, a two-tier architecture that assigns latency-critical interaction and proactive monitoring to independently scheduled frontend workers, while backend workers asynchronously construct persistent multimodal memory and perform historical recall and external search. StreamMind outperforms existing streaming baselines across all four capabilities and reduces query-to-answer latency by reusing persistent state.

</details>


### [42] [G$^2$ARD-GS: Geometry-Guided Anchor-Regularized Gaussian Splatting Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05704)
*Puyuan Zhang,Jianming Huang,Wenkai Ye,Wei Dong*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: G^2ARD-GS is a geometry-guided distillation method that compresses dense Gaussian splatting representations of LiDAR-derived maps into compact, surface-aware representations without changing topology during recovery. It achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction quality across 5×–30× compression budgets, outperforming PUP, and improves appearance adaptation and registration when used with frozen geometry.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Dense LiDAR maps yield city-scale geometry via 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) but consist of millions of primitives, making storage, transmission, rendering, and adaptation costly. Aggressive primitive reduction can degrade local surface support needed for robust novel-view synthesis and downstream geometric tasks. A compact, reusable representation that preserves geometry and supports appearance is highly desirable.

Method: G^2ARD-GS progressively consolidates a dense Gaussian prior (either a training-free point-cloud lift or a trained GS model) into surface-aware representatives. It recovers appearance on a fixed topology under construction-time anchor constraints, with no addition or removal of primitives during recovery. Under limited supervision, geometry-aware view selection allocates the available view budget.

Result: On MatrixCity, G^2ARD-GS achieves the best PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS across matched 5×–30× compression budgets, outperforming PUP by 3.2–6.8 dB in PSNR. When reused as frozen geometry, it improves off-trajectory appearance adaptation by 3.7–4.9 dB over PUP 3D-GS and preserves image-to-model registration accuracy on Cambridge Kings College at 30× compression.

Conclusion: G^2ARD-GS provides a geometry-guided path to compact, reusable priors for dense LiDAR-based 3D representations, balancing compression with geometric fidelity and appearance. It demonstrates strong, dataset-agnostic gains across budgets and enables efficient storage, transmission, and rendering while preserving registration and geometry.

Abstract: Dense colored LiDAR maps provide accurate city-scale geometry, but lifting them into 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) retains millions of primitives, making the resulting models costly to store, transmit, render, and adapt. Aggressive primitive reduction alleviates this burden, but can remove the local surface support needed for stable novel-view synthesis and downstream geometric use. We introduce G$^2$ARD-GS, a geometry-guided distillation method that converts a dense Gaussian prior instantiated either as a training-free point-cloud lift or a trained GS model into a compact, reusable representation. G$^2$ARD-GS progressively consolidates the prior into surface-aware representatives, then recovers appearance on the resulting fixed topology under construction-time anchor constraints, with no primitives added or removed during recovery. Under limited supervision, geometry-aware view selection allocates the available view budget. On MatrixCity, G$^2$ARD-GS achieves the best PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS across matched $5\times$--$30\times$ compression budgets, outperforming PUP by $3.2$--$6.8$,dB in PSNR. When reused as frozen geometry, the compact model improves off-trajectory appearance adaptation by $3.7$--$4.9$,dB over PUP 3D-GS and preserves image-to-model registration accuracy on Cambridge KingsCollege at $30\times$ compression. Project page: https://patrick1159.github.io/gardGS-page/.

</details>


### [43] [LAWM-3D: Learning 3D-Aware Latent Actions from Human Videos for Generalizable Robot World Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05706)
*Jiarui Yang,Jiale Zhange,Jiawei Li,Hang Guo,Wen Huang,Jinpeng Wang,Peidong Liu,Shu-Tao Xia*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Simply adding multi-view videos to latent action models does not yield 3D-aware latent actions due to future-frame leakage and cross-view discrepancies. LAWM-3D introduces tightly coupled designs to enforce 3D awareness and robust supervision, achieving SOTA in generation quality, physical consistency, and generalization after a two-stage pretraining/fine-tuning pipeline.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: LAMs trained on single-view 2D inputs struggle to generalize to open-world settings with diverse viewpoints and expensive action annotations. Multi-view data alone leads to appearance leakage and inconsistent cross-view cues, hindering 3D understanding in world models.

Method: Three coupled designs: (1) multi-view invariant unified action tokenization for consistent latent actions across views; (2) geometric alignment constraint linking encoder features to a pretrained 3D foundation model to provide cross-view correspondences; (3) a non-injective RGB-D joint reconstruction objective to prevent reliance on future-frame appearance and force learning of motion- and geometry-relevant cues. These are integrated in a two-stage pipeline: large-scale human video pretraining followed by robot fine-tuning.

Result: Extensive experiments show that 3D-aware latent actions improve world model performance substantially in generation quality, physical consistency, and generalization, achieving state-of-the-art results across these metrics.

Conclusion: Tightly coupled, 3D-aware latent action design with unified motivation and a two-stage training regime enables better 3D perception and planning in open-world embodied intelligence, outperforming prior LAMs that rely on 2D single-view inputs.

Abstract: World models enable agents to perform forward rollout and planning without real-world interaction. However, their application in open-world embodied intelligence remains limited by the high cost of action annotations and the heterogeneity of action spaces across platforms. Recently, latent action models (LAMs) have alleviated this bottleneck by learning action representations directly from unlabeled human videos in a self-supervised manner. Nevertheless, most existing LAMs rely on single-view inputs and operate primarily in 2D pixel space, raising a fundamental question: can simply incorporating multi-view videos into LAM training endow the learned latent actions with 3D-aware perception? Our study shows that the answer is negative. The primary reasons lie in future-frame appearance leakage as well as inter-camera appearance discrepancies and viewpoint variations. To address these issues, we propose LAWM-3D, which introduces three tightly coupled key designs: (1) a multi-view invariant unified action tokenization scheme for learning 3D-aware latent actions; (2) a geometric alignment constraint that anchors intermediate encoder features to a pretrained 3D foundation model, thereby explicitly providing cross-view geometric correspondences; and (3) a non-injective RGB-D joint reconstruction objective that prevents shortcut learning from future-frame appearance information, forcing the LAM to focus supervision on motion cues with geometric significance. Importantly, these components are not simply stacked but are tightly coupled through a unified motivation. Built upon a two-stage paradigm of large-scale human video pretraining followed by robot fine-tuning, extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed 3D-aware latent actions significantly improve world model performance, achieving SOTA results in generation quality, physical consistency, and generalization ability.

</details>


### [44] [One Ranking, Any Budget: Matryoshka Evidence-to-Context Frame Selection for Long-Video Understanding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05707)
*Wang Chen,Yu Chen,Xiang Wang,Shuai Li,Jinfa Huang,Xiawu Zheng*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: MEC introduces a training-free Matryoshka-style frame ranking for long-video selection, yielding a reusable prefix-friendly order that supports multiple budgets while preserving evidence and context.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Long videos have high frame redundancy and LMM context limits. Practical selectors must handle varying budgets across downstream tasks and latency constraints, and current methods optimize a single budget at a time, leading to churn when budgets change.

Method: MEC builds a reusable sparse video index, then uses sparse probing and local zooming to discover candidate frames. It greedily constructs a position-adaptive ranking (early positions = evidence, later positions = larger temporal coverage and diversity) so a single ranking can be truncated to any budget without recomputation.

Result: Across four benchmarks and six budgets, MEC improves average accuracy over uniform sampling by 3.77 percentage points, matches strong state-of-the-art selectors, and reduces end-to-end selection latency by 47.37-51.19%.

Conclusion: A training-free, prefix-friendly ranking framework enables efficient, budget-agnostic frame selection for long videos, achieving competitive accuracy with substantial latency reductions.

Abstract: Frame selection is essential for applying Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to long videos due to severe frame redundancy and limited context windows. Since the appropriate frame budget varies with the downstream LMM, reasoning demands, and latency constraints, a practical selector should serve multiple budgets. However, existing methods typically optimize an isolated frame subset for each predefined budget: when the budget changes, previously selected evidence may be replaced rather than progressively augmented. Ranking frames by a fixed score would allow prefix reuse across budgets, but it ignores the distinct roles of different ranking positions. In this paper, we formulate long-video frame selection as a Matryoshka ranking problem: constructing a single priority sequence whose small prefixes concentrate query-conditioned evidence, while progressively larger prefixes preserve this evidence and add broader temporal context. Efficiently constructing such a ranking is itself challenging, as densely sampling long videos and evaluating frame-query relevance incurs substantial overhead. We therefore introduce Matryoshka Evidence-to-Context (MEC) Frame Selection, a training-free framework that builds a reusable sparse video index, discovers candidates through sparse probing and local zooming, and greedily constructs a position-adaptive ranking: early positions emphasize evidence; later positions progressively favor temporal coverage while preserving visual diversity. A single ranking can thus be truncated to any target budget without rerunning the selector. Across four benchmarks and six frame budgets, MEC improves average accuracy over uniform sampling by 3.77 percentage points, matches strong state-of-the-art selectors, and reduces end-to-end selection latency by 47.37-51.19%.

</details>


### [45] [Iterative Hybrid Discrete-Continuous Viewpoint Planning for UAV Photogrammetry](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05718)
*Alan Grech,Daniel Pisani,Andre Grima,Carl James Debono,Saviour Formosa,Dylan Seychell*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Iterative hybrid discrete-continuous viewpoint planning for UAV photogrammetry targeting weakly observed regions using proxy reconstruction and CMA-ES optimization, improving accuracy and completeness over prior path-planning methods.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Conventional UAV flight patterns often fail to adapt to scene geometry, leading to local reconstruction errors; robust coverage, overlap, parallax, and surface resolution require better viewpoint planning.

Method: Score sampled surface points with photogrammetric heuristics (frontality, imaging distance, parallax, multi-view observation count) and evaluate the full viewpoint set for visibility, pairwise overlap, and graph connectivity. Generate candidate viewpoints around weakly observed regions, refine via clustered CMA-ES optimization, and remove redundant viewpoints. Final flight path blends close-range detail viewpoints with wider model-coverage viewpoints to balance local quality and global image-network robustness.

Result: Evaluation on three synthetic scenes shows improved reconstruction accuracy and completeness compared with prior UAV path-planning methods.

Conclusion: The method achieves a balance between local reconstruction quality and global network robustness in UAV photogrammetry; validated on synthetic data with potential for real-world validation and extension.

Abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) photogrammetry requires camera networks that provide sufficient surface coverage, image overlap, parallax, and resolution, yet conventional flight patterns are often poorly adapted to scene geometry resulting in local reconstruction errors. This paper proposes an iterative hybrid discrete-continuous viewpoint planning method for targeted UAV photogrammetry from a proxy reconstruction. The method scores sampled surface points using photogrammetric heuristics based on frontality, imaging distance, parallax, and multi-view observation count, while also evaluating the full viewpoint set in terms of visibility, pairwise overlap, and graph connectivity. Candidate viewpoints are generated around weakly observed regions, refined using clustered Covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES) optimisation, and removed when redundant. The final flight path combines close-range detail viewpoints with wider model-coverage viewpoints, balancing local reconstruction quality with global image-network robustness. Evaluation on three synthetic scenes shows that the proposed method improves both reconstruction accuracy and completeness compared with prior UAV path-planning methods.

</details>


### [46] [PhyLatent: Learning Dynamics-Relevant Representations for JEPA World Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05720)
*Xi Zeng,Haojie Ren,Ziying Song*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: PhyLatent introduces three training pathways to address JEPA world model failure modes (physical invariance, identifiability, and counterfactual dynamics), improving latent state fidelity and dynamics; empirical gains on OGBench-Cube, TwoRooms, and competitive results elsewhere show that preventing global latent collapse alone is insufficient for robust JEPA worldmodels.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Global latent non-collapse does not guarantee preservation of physical states and action consequences; JEPA-based world models suffer from three distinct failure modes that undermine reliable state-space learning and planning.

Method: Three training pathways: physical invariance (physical state grounding, static visual invariance), physical identifiability (future representation alignment), and counterfactual dynamics (counterfactual branch separation, latent denoising). Implemented to prevent physical invariance collapse, physical identifiability collapse, and counterfactual dynamics collapse.

Result: On OGBench-Cube, three failure rates drop from 15.60%, 6.71%, 8.41% to 7.53%, 0.95%, 4.62% respectively; MPC success rises from 70.0% to 78.1%. Using the same architecture and planner, TwoRooms MPC success improves from 81.0% to 98.0%; performance on Reacher and PushT remains competitive.

Conclusion: Global non-collapse is insufficient for learning a reliable JEPA world-model state space; targeted training objectives addressing the identified failure modes yield substantial gains in state fidelity and planning success.

Abstract: We propose PhyLatent, a dynamics-relevant training objective for JointEmbedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models. Our key observation is that preventing global latent collapse does not ensure that a representation preserves physical states and action consequences. We identify three failure modes in JEPA world models: physical invariance collapse, physical identifiability collapse, and counterfactual dynamics collapse. PhyLatent addresses them through three training pathways: physical invariance, physical identifiability, and counterfactual dynamics, implemented with physical state grounding, future representation alignment, static visual invariance, counterfactual branch separation, and latent denoising. On OGBench-Cube, PhyLatent reduces the three failure rates from 15.60%, 6.71%, and 8.41% to 7.53%, 0.95%, and 4.62%, respectively, and improves model predictive control (MPC) success from 70.0% to 78.1%. With the same architecture and planner, it further improves success from 81.0% to 98.0% on TwoRooms and remains competitive on Reacher and PushT. These results show that global non-collapse alone is insufficient for learning a reliable JEPA worldmodel state space.

</details>


### [47] [Engram-E2VID: Reference-Based Event-to-Video Reconstruction via Generative Activation of Appearance Engrams](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05728)
*Feiyu Ji,Xiang Li,Hao Ma,Tianxiang Huang,Qingxin Lu,Mengqi Ji,Lei Han,Xiaokang Yang,Xiaoyun Yuan*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Engram-E2VID introduces a structure-guided, diffusion-based framework for reference-based event-to-video reconstruction that uses token-space appearance engrams derived from a reference frame and a target-time motion-structure scaffold from events and context to progressively activate appearance engrams. This yields improved reconstruction quality over baselines, especially on longer intervals.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Reconstructing target RGB frames from a reference frame and asynchronous, sparse event data is challenging because events encode changes rather than absolute appearance. The key difficulty is associating event-driven temporal structures with appropriate appearance information, particularly under complex motion and long temporal gaps.

Method: Encode the reference frame into token-space appearance engrams. Transform the event stream and reference context into a target-time motion-structure scaffold that captures motion boundaries and event-induced changes. Use a one-step diffusion backbone where scaffold-derived structural tokens interact with appearance engrams across layers, enabling token-space association of target structures with reference appearance without pixel-wise alignment. The diffusion prior helps recover uncertain or newly revealed regions.

Result: On three benchmarks, PSNR improves by up to 3.29 dB and LPIPS improves by up to 0.08 over the strongest same-input baseline, with slower degradation as the reconstruction interval increases.

Conclusion: The structure-guided, diffusion-based framework enables effective cross-structure transfer from the reference to target frames via appearance engrams, improving reconstruction quality for reference-based event-to-video tasks and showing robustness to longer intervals.

Abstract: Reference-based event-to-video reconstruction aims to recover target RGB frames from a reference frame and the event stream captured over the reference-to-target interval. Although events provide fine-grained temporal cues, they encode sparse and asynchronous log-intensity changes rather than absolute appearance, making faithful reconstruction intrinsically challenging. The central challenge lies in associating event-derived target-time structures with relevant appearance information from the reference frame, especially under complex motion and long temporal intervals. In this work, we propose Engram-E2VID, a structure-guided framework that reconstructs target frames through the generative activation of appearance engrams. Specifically, the reference frame is encoded into token-space appearance engrams, while the event stream and reference context are transformed into a target-time motion-structure scaffold that captures motion boundaries and event-induced structural changes. Within a one-step diffusion backbone, scaffold-derived structural tokens progressively interact with and activate relevant appearance engrams across layers. This token-space association allows target structures to access reference appearance without relying on direct pixel-wise correspondence, while the diffusion prior complements uncertain or newly revealed regions. Across three benchmarks, Engram-E2VID improves PSNR by up to 3.29 dB and reduces LPIPS by up to 0.08 over the strongest same-input baseline, while degrading more slowly as the reconstruction interval increases.

</details>


### [48] [LiteKD-Net: Lightweight Knowledge-Distilled Network for Mobile Image Denoising](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05739)
*Zhou Zhiyi*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: LiteKD-Net proposes a lightweight, knowledge-distilled denoiser for mobile imaging, using physics-guided noise simulation, a Real-ESRGAN-based lightweight Student with Lite-RRDB blocks, and feature-level distillation; claims state-of-the-art metrics vs SwinIR with lower runtime.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Mobile image denoising requires high restoration quality with low compute and lacks large-scale LQ-GT pairs; a method combining data synthesis, efficient architecture, and knowledge distillation could address both data scarcity and efficiency.

Method: 1) Physics-guided noise simulation adding pixel crosstalk to generate paired data; 2) Adapt Real-ESRGAN for identity-resolution denoising; build lightweight Student using Lite-RRDB blocks with depthwise separable convolutions; 3) apply feature-level knowledge distillation from Teacher to Student without extra inference cost.

Result: Experiments on real-world datasets show significant runtime reduction and higher inference rate with preserving restoration quality; reports best metrics compared to SwinIR.

Conclusion: LiteKD-Net achieves a strong accuracy-efficiency trade-off for mobile image denoising, leveraging data synthesis, architecture efficiency, and distillation.

Abstract: Mobile image denoising requires both good restoration quality and low computational cost. In addition, it's annoying to collect large-scale LQ-GT clean pairs. As a result, we propose LiteKD-Net, a lightweight knowledge-distilled network for mobile image denoising. First, a physics-guided noise simulation pipeline generates paired training data by adding pixel crosstalk compared with pipelines applied to cameras. Next, we adapt the Real-ESRGAN to identity-resolution denoising and construct a lightweight Student using Lite-RRDB blocks based on depthwise separable convolutions. Third, feature-level knowledge distillation is applied to transfer the Teacher's restoration capability to the Student without introducing additional inference cost. Experiments on real-world datasets show that our model reaches great reduction in runtime and increase in the inference rate with good restoration quality. Our model also reaches the best in all metrics compared with SwinIR. These results indicate that LiteKD-Net provides a great trade-off between restoration quality and computational efficiency.

</details>


### [49] [ConceptADapt: Concept-guided Adaptive Feature Reconstruction with Dynamic Attention for Few-Shot Industrial Anomaly Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05743)
*Yufei Li,Yicheng Ruan,Long Tian,Dongsheng Wang,Liang Bao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ConceptADapt uses fixed normal concepts extracted from few support samples and dynamic attention with sparse autoencoders, plus LoRA, to improve few-shot industrial anomaly detection (FS-IAD); shows state-of-the-art results on MVTec-AD, VisA, MPDD across various shot settings.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: FS-IAD struggles due to extreme data scarcity for normal samples; foundation-model features help but generalization remains fragile without robust adaptation. The work addresses feature shortcut and fast adaptation in a lightweight framework.

Method: Pre-learns a set of fixed normal concepts from limited support features; uses them to relate to query features and recalibrate statistics for anomaly detection. Introduces a dynamic attention mechanism with sparse autoencoders to learn robust normal concepts during training, mitigating feature shortcut. Employs LoRA in the attention module for lightweight, fast adaptation during inference.

Result: Extensive experiments on three FS-IAD benchmarks (MVTec-AD, VisA, MPDD) show the method consistently outperforms SOTA on both detection and localization across multiple shot settings.

Conclusion: ConceptADapt provides a concept-guided adaptive reconstruction framework with dynamic attention and efficient adaptation (LoRA) to achieve robust FS-IAD under data scarcity, with strong empirical gains on standard benchmarks.

Abstract: Few-shot industrial anomaly detection (FS-IAD) focuses on detecting and localizing visual defects in industrial inspection during the cold-start phase, where only a limited number of normal training samples are available per category. Recent advances in this field predominantly leverage visual features from foundation-model and have achieved promising performance. Despite the strong representational power of foundation-model features, the model generalization remains fragile due to the extreme scarcity of normal training data.To address this pivotal issue, we propose ConceptADapt, a concept-guided adaptive feature reconstruction model with dynamic attention. Specifically, our model pre-learns a set of fixed normal concepts from the limited support features and leverages them to mine relationships with query features, thereby recalibrating their statistics for improved anomaly detection at test time. To mitigate the prevalent feature shortcut problem, which is particularly severe under low-data regimes, we further develop a dynamic attention mechanism integrated with sparse autoencoders to learn robust normal concepts during training. Moreover, to enable fast adaptation during inference, our model remains lightweight by incorporating LoRA into the attention module, which introduces only minimal updating parameters.Extensive experiments on three widely adopted FS-IAD benchmarks, including MVTec-AD, VisA, and MPDD, demonstrate that our model consistently outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) approaches across both detection and localization tasks, achieving significant improvements under various shot settings.

</details>


### [50] [UniVVT: A Unified End-to-End Framework for High-Fidelity Video Virtual Try-on](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05745)
*Yushe Cao,Shikun Feng,Fei Shen,Haikuo Peng,Jianqiang Xia,Yiheng Zhu,Dianxi Shi,Chun Yu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: UniVVT delivers end-to-end video virtual try-on by semantically conditioning a diffusion-based video generator with a scene-task perceiver, achieving state-of-the-art without explicit mask/pose/warping modules.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Conventional VVT pipelines rely on multi-stage, geometrically explicit priors (masking, pose estimation, warping). These components propagate errors and complicate deployment; an end-to-end, semantically guided approach can improve robustness and simplicity.

Method: Introduce UniVVT: a unified end-to-end framework using a scene-task perceiver based on a Multimodal LLM to encode source video, target garment, and task instructions into latent tokens. A lightweight semantic bridge aligns these tokens with the diffusion-based video generator's conditioning space. Employ a three-stage training regime—semantic alignment, joint task adaptation, and flexible-resolution refinement—to robustly fuse heterogeneous components and enable inference without separate geometry modules.

Result: Extensive experiments show state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks, validating that implicit semantic guidance can replace fragile geometric preprocessing for end-to-end VVT.

Conclusion: Implicit semantic guidance via a scene-task perceiver is an effective alternative to explicit geometric priors, enabling simpler, more robust end-to-end video virtual try-on.

Abstract: Video Virtual Try-On (VVT) synthesizes a video of a person wearing a target garment while preserving identity, motion, and scene dynamics. Dominant approaches cast VVT as mask-conditioned video inpainting and rely on separate modules for human parsing, pose estimation, and garment warping. This multi-stage design complicates deployment and, more critically, allows errors in explicit geometric priors to propagate irreversibly into the generated video. We present UniVVT, a unified end-to-end framework that reframes VVT as semantically conditioned video generation, eliminating mask, pose, and warping modules at inference. At its core, a scene-task perceiver built on a Multimodal Large Language Model jointly encodes the source video, target garment, and task instruction into compact, task-aware latent tokens, implicitly capturing what to transfer and where and how to transfer it. A lightweight semantic bridge then aligns these tokens with the conditioning space of a diffusion-based video generator, enabling coherent garment transfer. To robustly couple the heterogeneous components, we devise a three-stage progressive training strategy comprising semantic alignment, joint task adaptation, and flexible-resolution refinement. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UniVVT achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks, validating implicit semantic guidance as a simple and effective alternative to fragile geometric preprocessing for end-to-end virtual try-on.

</details>


### [51] [GST-Bench: Can VLMs Develop Global Spatial Awareness from Video?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05747)
*Qifeng Zhang,Kaixiang Huang,Heng Dong,Huang Fang,Junting Chen,Junjie Zhu,Yonghang Chen,Zhiyu Zhang,Wei Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A benchmark suite (GST-Bench) for global spatial intelligence in video VQA, revealing a substantial gap between state-of-the-art models and humans. It introduces GST-Bench-Local and GST-Train to diagnose and facilitate global, long-horizon spatial reasoning beyond local perception.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current benchmarks emphasize local spatial understanding from limited viewpoints, neglecting global spatial awareness across continuous, long-horizon video streams; there is a need for evaluation and data to push models toward consistent global scene representations from egocentric inputs.
